title: Selection on the family explains traits of sterile social-insect workers

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Selection on the family explains traits of sterile social-insect workers

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Traits of sterile workers in social insects can evolve because selection acts on the family: fertile parents whose colonies produce sterile members with a useful modification flourish and transmit the tendency to produce such members.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: selection may be applied to the family, as well as to the individual, and may thus gain the desired end.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter VII, “Instinct”; section “Neuter or sterile insects”. Scope: social insects with sterile castes (ants, bees, wasps, termites)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch07-12: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.78

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern quantitative genetics and social-evolution data directly establish how sterile-worker traits respond to selection through relatives. Broad taxonomic coverage is imperfect but sufficient to resolve the mechanism.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Estimate heritability of worker traits through reproductive parents and test whether colony reproductive output increases with those traits. A genetic association transmitted by breeders plus colony-level fitness effects supports family selection.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Colony fitness and pedigree data are concentrated in model species.

Kin and multilevel-selection parameterizations can describe the same process.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.76
data adequacy: 0.68
data existence: 0.86
analysis feasibility: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.88

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Genomes and caste lists make the genetic precondition of family selection testable in well-studied social insects. The relatedness and fitness data that would show selection on parents, rather than an alternative social mechanism, still have to be compiled. The scope includes all social insects with sterile castes, and public data match only a subset.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Test whether worker traits segregate in the parental genome and whether sterile castes evolve where within-colony relatedness is high. Parental transmission of worker phenotypes supports family-level selection; worker adaptations that cannot be transmitted by fertile parents, or that evolve where relatedness is too low for that pathway, would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Colony relatedness estimates are scattered in papers, not in AntWeb or GenBank.

Termites and many wasps are poorly represented relative to honeybees and a few ant genera.

Haplodiploidy and manipulation hypotheses make similar predictions about sterile workers.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

operationalizability: 0.66
analysis feasibility: 0.48
data adequacy: 0.45
data existence: 0.55
